analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Nov 6 Stainless steels warning, Flat steel calm, Copper continues to cut Mkt colour from GS on Yday moves
key_insights: Copper is more than $1,000 below its highs while physical stocks sit at lows. The desk says equity flows were all risk-related, with overnight shorting of copper against gold. Gold's weakness is described as a trim to overall positioning.
Codelco's Andina halted mine processing (175kt) after what appears to be a modest tailings spill, described as precautionary. This is the latest copper supply disruption.
The desk says the market is 'ultra complacent' on copper supply. Weather impacts on Q4 output (Lundin, Antofagasta) should lower Q4 actuals and likely lead to 2027 trims with a lag.

European stainless steel outlook is weak. Outokumpu guides Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA to a level similar to the EUR 10m of Q4 2025, versus consensus of EUR 102m, and the stock opened -16%. Aperam missed modestly with adj EBITDA of 105m (cons 107.5), -18% q/q.

European flat steel has sponsorship from tariffs and a pickup in domestic utilisation. ArcelorMittal (MT.NA) says European apparent demand and order books are strengthening materially on trade protection and import displacement, and that destocking is ending. GSe sees European flat steel shipment growth of +20%.

The desk is cautious on calling a 'recovery trade' in steel after the weak tape, but says that is how it is seen, with upgrades at spot. The desk will start down with the space but expects to rel o/p.
Annual 2027 contract benchmarks for steel and copper are being set at a volatile time, with copper benchmarks set around CESCO week in late November.
Nickel has rallied strongly. Indonesia reportedly has three nickel firms planning 2027 output cuts, and the minister said 'If prices are currently not high or favorable, then leave it in the ground.'
China property tour feedback shows a cautious consensus on domestic macro demand and low expectations for policy support, with supply contraction and quality improvement key to stabilization.

GS estimates October NFP at +75k (consensus 65k), average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m (cons 0.3%) and unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. GS sees risks skewed toward a lower reading, reflecting possible convergence to the lower level implied by continuing claims.

Goldman's prime brokerage desk says global fundamental long/short managers fell 1.3% (a -2 SD move), TMT funds fell more than 4% and are roughly flat YTD versus about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off. Momentum fell 3.7 SD for multi-strats.

On the US session, NDX fell 6.36% (worst day since March 9, 2020), S&P fell 4.36% and SOX fell 12%. High beta momentum fell 6.2%, 51% off its June highs. Asset managers were net sellers of semis/AI with no offsetting bid for hyperscalers/defensive tech.

Vol spiked. VVIX rose nearly 45 points (second largest one-day rise ever), VIX moved above 26, and the GS Vol Panic Index reached 9.3/10. Skew steepened and front-end fixed strike vols were bid aggressively. The desk expects incremental US systematic supply, estimated at -$7.48bn of S&P for sale over the next week, after futures closed below the 7549 CTA threshold.

Gold miners: Gold Fields kept FY26 guidance of 2.4-2.6Moz. AngloGold production was down and costs up on Africa disruptions. Aura Minerals Q3 was in line. Energy Fuels is targeting the low end of 2026 uranium sales guidance. EDP's 9M net profit was EUR 1.2bn with possible upside to its FY guide of EUR 1.4bn.

market_movers.rationale: Outokumpu opened -16% after guiding Q4 2026 adj EBITDA to a level similar to the EUR 10m of Q4 2025, versus EUR 102m consensus. Q3 EBITDA was 101m vs cons 99m.
Aperam missed modestly with adj EBITDA of 105m vs cons 107.5m, down 18% q/q. Guidance is for slightly higher q/q but implies cuts of roughly 20-25% in the region.

ArcelorMittal says European apparent demand and order books are strengthening on trade protection, destocking is ending, and North America is fully booked for Q4. GSe sees European flat steel shipments +20%.
Lundin Mining flagged extreme weather and lower October production, with haulage speeds down 20% at Caserones. GS cut 2026-27 EBITDA estimates by 3%/5%.
Gold Fields kept FY26 guidance of 2.4-2.6Moz with confidence in the upper end. GS lowers 2026-27 EBITDA by 2%/1% and assumes Tarkwa licences are renewed on less favourable fiscal terms.
AngloGold production was down and costs up, with the miss concentrated in Africa (flooding at Iduapriem, Obuasi recovery, a rockfall and fatality at Sukari).
Energy Fuels' Q3 uranium sales and mined volumes were below GS expectations. The company targets the low end of 2026 sales guidance and GS 2026-2028 adj EBITDA moves to ($79mn)/($4mn)/$25mn.

sector_views.rationale: Tariffs, import displacement, domestic utilisation pickup and the end of destocking support the group, though the desk expects to start down on the day.
Outokumpu and Aperam point to weak European demand, high inventory and no substantial spot base-price increases.
Supply disruptions and weather are likely to cut Q4 actuals and 2027 estimates, but copper has sold off on risk-related flows.

earnings_insights: Aperam reported adj EBITDA of EUR 105m vs consensus EUR 107.5m, down 18% q/q. Guidance is for slightly higher q/q.
Outokumpu reported Q3 adj EBITDA of EUR 101m vs consensus EUR 99m. Q4 2026 adj EBITDA is guided to a level similar to the EUR 10m recorded in Q4 2025, versus consensus of EUR 102m.
Lundin Mining (call held 11/6): GS lowers 2026-27 EBITDA estimates by 3%/5% on Sep-quarter actuals, a more conservative production outlook and higher operating costs.
Gold Fields reported FY26 guidance of 2.4-2.6Moz unchanged. GS lowers 2026-27 EBITDA by 2%/1%.
AngloGold Ashanti reported lower production and higher costs, with the miss concentrated in Africa.
Aura Minerals Q3 was in line. 4Q26 is expected to be the strongest quarter at 100k oz, against FY guidance of 340-390k oz.

Energy Fuels Q3 uranium sales and mined volumes were below GS expectations, partly offset by better realized pricing. Management targets the low end of 2026 uranium sales guidance. GS 2026-2028 adj EBITDA estimates are ($79mn)/($4mn)/$25mn versus prior ($52mn)/($6mn)/$25mn.
EDP 9M net profit was EUR 1.2bn. Excluding EUR 200m of AR gains, the run rate is EUR 300-350m per quarter, implying upside risk to FY guidance of EUR 1.4bn.
Hua Hong Q3 net income rose 222.39% q/q and Q4 sales guidance beat estimates. The stock ended the morning +8.37%.

trade_ideas.description: Trade the European steel space down on the day, then go relative outperformer on flat steel versus stainless
trade_ideas.rationale: Flat steel has sponsorship from tariffs and a domestic utilisation pickup, while stainless faces weak demand and high inventory.

risk_factors: Further copper supply disruptions (Andina, Caserones, Los Pelambres) with the market complacent on Q4 and 2027 estimates.
Weak European steel demand and high inventory, with Outokumpu guiding Q4 EBITDA down more than 90% y/y.
Systematic and CTA supply after futures closed below 7549, estimated at -$7.48bn of S&P over the next week.
Payrolls risk skewed lower, reflecting possible convergence to the lower level implied by continuing claims.
Gold Fields: uncertainty on Tarkwa licence timing, future value sharing and the economic framework.
Volatile pricing around annual contract benchmark negotiations for steel and copper.
vol_and_positioning: VVIX rose nearly 45 points, the second largest one-day move higher ever behind Volmageddon. Nasdaq's VIX had its largest one-day change since COVID and VIX spiked above 26.
GS Vol Panic Index (1m S&P implied vol, VIX vol, S&P 1m skew, term structure slope) reached 9.3 out of 10 intraday.
Hedge monetization dominated early flows in S&P, Nasdaq and VIX. Skew steepened sharply and front-end fixed strike NDX and SPX vols were bid aggressively.
GS customer bought 22k SPY 27Nov 700/730 put spreads. VIX calls and call spreads were unwound as the index spiked above 26.
Implied move through tomorrow is 1.43%. The straddle through the end of the week was 91bps at the prior close.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549). The desk expects incremental US supply, with a -2.5 stdev estimate of -$7.48bn of S&P for sale over the next week.
ETFs had their largest share of volume since June, at 32% of the tape. Asset managers were net sellers, hedge fund flows were roughly balanced with short books toggled aggressively.
High beta momentum fell 6.2% and is 51% off its June highs, its worst drawdown in more than 10 years.
geopolitical: Trade policy protection and import displacement are cited as driving European steel demand, and the US/Canada steel arb does not currently incentivise Canada to export to the US.
Concerns that Democrats may tighten regulation of the AI industry in the US, which some argue could speed up China's domestic semiconductor substitution.
Indonesia's nickel firms plan 2027 output cuts, with the minister saying to leave nickel in the ground if prices are not favorable.
Ghana's Tarkwa licence renewal is the base case, with higher royalties from 2Q'27 and elevated uncertainty on timing and fiscal terms.

tension_points.bull_case: Tariffs, import displacement and a domestic utilisation pickup support European flat steel. ArcelorMittal says order books are strengthening materially and destocking is ending, with GSe at +20% shipment growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Outokumpu and Aperam cite sluggish European demand, high inventory and weak volumes, with Outokumpu guiding Q4 EBITDA down more than 90% y/y.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weak Q4 volumes and no substantial spot base-price increases as the 2027 contract tonnes are negotiated.
